one_liner: Online payments, billing, invoicing and financial infrastructure APIs for businesses.
auth_notes: Secret keys (sk_test_/sk_live_) or restricted keys (rk_live_, recommended) sent as HTTP Basic username or as Bearer token. Connect OAuth (connect.stripe.com/oauth) exists for platforms but platforms must request read_write; read_only is only for extensions/Stripe Apps, and returned access_token is deprecated in favour of platform key + Stripe-Account header. Workload Identity Federation also available. Stripe MCP uses its own OAuth or 'agent API keys'.
access_notes: Anyone can create a Stripe account and immediately get test-mode/sandbox keys at $0. Live mode requires account activation (business verification), which is normal onboarding rather than developer gating.
api_breadth_notes: Hundreds of operations across payments, customers, billing/subscriptions, invoices, Connect, Issuing, Treasury/money management, Radar, Tax, Checkout, payment links, webhooks/events; MCP page alone lists ~170 supported API methods.
mcp_notes: Official remote server https://mcp.stripe.com (Streamable HTTP), OAuth via Stripe consent page or agent API key as Bearer; tools include stripe_api_read/stripe_api_write covering most of the API, docs search, analytics. From Jan 11, 2027 MCP will no longer accept full secret keys or non-agent restricted keys.
notes: Best end-user path is a restricted API key per account; a public OAuth app would go through Stripe Apps (read_only scope) rather than legacy Connect OAuth. Some MCP actions (refunds, Treasury transfers) require human confirmation in the Dashboard. OAuth MCP sessions expire after 14 days.

one_liner: Connects apps to users' bank accounts for balances, transactions, identity and payments.
auth_notes: client_id + secret from the Plaid Dashboard, sent in JSON body or PLAID-CLIENT-ID/PLAID-SECRET headers. End-user data access requires a per-Item access_token obtained by running Plaid Link (client-side UI) and exchanging a public_token. Dashboard MCP uses OAuth client_credentials (/oauth/token, scope mcp:dashboard).
access_notes: Sandbox is always free (test Items only). Production requires requesting Production access in the Dashboard (company/application profile; OAuth-institution access also needs security questionnaire). New US/CA teams (since Apr 15, 2026) can apply for a free Trial plan capped at 10 Production Items; beyond that pay-as-you-go, Growth or Custom plans; EU/UK only Custom.
api_breadth_notes: POST/JSON API across many products (Auth, Transactions, Identity, Balance, Assets, Investments, Liabilities, Transfer, etc.); API overview page did not enumerate counts, but an OpenAPI spec and Postman collection are published.
mcp_notes: Two official servers: remote Dashboard MCP at https://api.dashboard.plaid.com/mcp/ (production diagnostics/analytics only: debug Item, Link analytics, usage; requires Production approval; OAuth client_credentials bearer, 15-min tokens) and a local 'AI coding toolkit' MCP for Sandbox/dev (mock data, docs search, webhook simulation). Neither exposes end-user financial data.
blocker: Production access needs Dashboard application; end users must link via Plaid Link
notes: Toolkit can be built and tested fully in Sandbox. Agent use is awkward because each bank connection needs the interactive Plaid Link flow to create an Item/access_token. Fetch of support.plaid.com article on Sandbox vs Production vs Trial failed (403); approval details partly from search snippets. Launch Checklist page says it is superseded by the Dashboard Launch Center.

one_liner: Cryptocurrency exchange with spot, margin, futures trading, wallet and market-data APIs.
auth_notes: X-MBX-APIKEY header plus signed requests (timestamp + signature) using HMAC-SHA256, RSA (PKCS#8) or Ed25519 (recommended) keys; key permissions scoped (TRADE, USER_DATA, USER_STREAM); public market data needs no key. Binance Login (OAuth2) exists but is only for close ecosystem partners.
access_notes: API keys are created by the account holder on the Binance API Management page at no cost (trading must be enabled per key). OAuth2 'Binance Login' is partner-only (contact business team). Account eligibility/KYC and regional restrictions not verified in fetched pages.
api_breadth_notes: Spot REST + WebSocket API + streams, plus separate margin, USD-M/COIN-M futures, wallet, sub-account and other product APIs; well over 100 operations across products (only Spot pages fetched).
mcp_notes: Official hosted 'Binance MCP Server (Agentic)' at https://agent.binance.com/mcp/agentic; consent-screen auth, no local API keys; trades only inside a dedicated, manually funded Agentic sub-account; scopes market data/account/trade/transfer, no withdrawals. Many community MCP servers also exist (e.g. PyPI binance-mcp-server).
blocker: End-user OAuth is partner-only; toolkit must hold raw signed keys
notes: Events are delivered via WebSocket user-data streams, not HTTP webhooks. Spot Testnet and Demo Mode appear in docs navigation (not opened). Rate limits are per IP with escalating IP bans (418) on abuse, which matters for a shared toolkit backend. Trading tools move real funds; consider read-only key scopes by default.

one_liner: NMI-powered payment gateway offering payments, subscriptions and marketplace split payments (Connect).
auth_notes: No Paygent-specific API reference found. Underlying NMI gateway uses security keys (private for server, public for client) sent as 'Authorization: <key>' (REST) or api_key body field (Classic). Paygent marketing site shows sample 'Authorization: Bearer pgt_live_xxx' against api.paygent.com/v1, but that host did not respond.
access_notes: Live keys come from a merchant account activated through Paygent/NMI (merchant approval required per site content). NMI offers sandbox keys via guide.nmi.com; Paygent site FAQ claims a free sandbox with full API access.
api_breadth_notes: NMI APIs: Payment API v5 (sale/auth/capture/void/refund), Customer Vault, Recurring (plans/subscriptions), Invoicing, Products, Query/reporting, Webhooks, Merchant onboarding; roughly 30-60 operations.
mcp_notes: No Paygent MCP found. NMI publishes an official local MCP (@nmipayments/nmi-mcp, 2 read-only tools: fetch_by_type, preflight; merchant API key; NMI_API_BASE_URL overridable) plus a docs MCP; unverified whether it works with Paygent-issued keys.
blocker: No Paygent-specific API docs; live keys need approved merchant account
notes: Vendor site https://www.gopaygent.com/ is a JS SPA (fetched; no readable docs). Its sitemap points to paygent.transactiongateway.com (NMI white-label gateway domain), whose /developers/docs and /products/connect returned 403. Site bundle references NMI merchant activation, Pathfinder API, Collect.js and Three-Step Redirect (all NMI products), so a toolkit would likely target NMI's gateway API with a per-merchant security key and a per-tenant gateway host. Name collides with unrelated Japanese gateway 'Paygent' and AI-billing 'Paygent' products. Confirm with vendor before building.

one_liner: FX audit service detecting hidden bank currency-conversion markups versus mid-market rates.
auth_notes: API keys (ipx_live_ / ipx_test_ prefixes) or Supabase JWT sent as Authorization: Bearer; generated in the iPayX dashboard. Some endpoints (spot rate, ROI calculator) allow anonymous calls.
access_notes: Developers page lists API plans from $99/mo (Developer: 100 audits, sandbox) up to $4,999/mo and Enterprise; signup is self-serve. Free allowances exist (3 lifetime web audits; MCP doc claims free tier of 10 audits/day per key; OpenAPI has 402 'free-tier quota exhausted'), so a $0 key may be possible - docs are inconsistent.
api_breadth_notes: 3 operations in OpenAPI (fx-audit-engine, fetch-spot-rate, roi-calculator); /docs/api lists a different 3 (POST /audit, GET /rates, POST /audit/document).
mcp_notes: Vendor-hosted MCP; llms.txt gives https://mcp.ipayx.ai/mcp (Streamable HTTP) while /docs/mcp-server gives a Supabase functions URL (.../functions/v1/mcp-server). Tools: audit_fx_transaction, check_fx_mid_market_rate, compare_fx_sources, full_forensic_fx_report (paid). Bearer API key auth.
blocker: API plans from $99/mo; inconsistent base URLs and endpoint docs
notes: Hinted URL ipayx.ai/docs is a 404; real docs at www.ipayx.ai/docs/api, /docs/mcp-server, /llms.txt and /.well-known/openapi.json. Small vendor (FINTRAC MSB claim is self-reported). Webhook audit.completed is HMAC-SHA256 signed (x-ipayx-signature). API is hosted on Supabase edge functions; base URLs differ across docs, so pin to the OpenAPI spec and verify before building. Pricing page shows consumer packs ($99 credits, $299/mo unlimited) distinct from API plans.

one_liner: Small-business accounting: invoicing, bills, payments, expenses and financial reports.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code via an app registered on the Intuit Developer Portal; per-company realmId; refresh tokens rotate on each refresh (about 100-day window). Sandbox accepts localhost redirect URIs; production requires a public HTTPS redirect.
access_notes: Free Intuit developer account with sandbox companies. Production keys are unlocked only after completing the per-app App Assessment Questionnaire and compliance profile. Intuit App Partner Program: Builder tier $0 with 500k metered CorePlus (read) calls/month (blocked after cap); Silver/Gold/Platinum paid tiers; Premium APIs (e.g. Projects) Silver+ only (third-party figures).
api_breadth_notes: Accounting API covers ~29+ entities (customers, invoices, bills, vendors, payments, deposits, journal entries, items, accounts, etc.) with CRUD/query plus ~11 financial reports; Intuit's MCP exposes 145 tools.
mcp_notes: Official open-source local stdio server github.com/intuit/quickbooks-online-mcp-server (OAuth2 via your own Intuit app; 145 tools; write/update/delete can be disabled). A hosted Intuit connector (ai-inc.quickbooks.intuit.com/v1/mcp) was reported in search results but not verified.
blocker: Production keys require Intuit app assessment questionnaire approval
notes: developer.intuit.com pages (OAuth guide, partner FAQ) are JS-rendered and returned no content via fetch, so access details come from third-party sources (Codat questionnaire guide; Apideck blog https://www.apideck.com/blog/quickbooks-api-pricing-and-the-intuit-app-partner-program). Webhooks confirmed only via search snippets (developer dashboard-configured, CloudEvents format migration). Read-heavy agent usage is metered as CorePlus calls; budget for partner tier at scale.

one_liner: Cloud accounting for small businesses: invoicing, bank reconciliation, payroll and reporting.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code (PKCE supported) with per-organisation consent; one app can connect multiple orgs (tenant selected per call). Custom Connections (client-credentials style, single org) also exist. Granular scopes per API area.
access_notes: Starter tier is free with no payment method: 5 connections, 1,000 calls/org/day. Core $35 AUD/mo (50 connections), Plus $245 (1,000, App Certification), Advanced $1,445 (10,000, certification + security assessment), Enterprise POA (App Store listing). Journals endpoint, XPM API and bulk connections need security assessment and use-case approval.
api_breadth_notes: Accounting API (accounts, contacts, invoices, bills, payments, bank transactions, journals, reports) plus Payroll, Files, Assets, Projects and other APIs; local MCP alone exposes 51 commands.
mcp_notes: Official remote MCP https://api.xero.com/mcp/v1 (OAuth2 PKCE; Core plan and above for real orgs, Starter limited to demo org; Custom Connections not eligible). Also official local open-source server XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server (npm @xeroapi/xero-mcp-server; custom connection or bearer token; 51 tools).
blocker: Free tier capped at 5 connections; scale needs paid tier plus certification
notes: developer.xero.com OAuth guide pages returned only titles via fetch, and the MCP how-to guide returned 'Not Authorized', so OAuth detail is taken from the Remote MCP FAQ and the MCP README. Sandbox = Xero Demo Company. Webhooks (signed, thin payloads; mainly invoices/contacts, credit notes reportedly added 2026) confirmed only via search snippets. Egress (data download) is metered per tier; review Xero developer terms on AI use of data before launch (not checked).

one_liner: Corporate cards, spend management, bill pay and business banking for companies.
auth_notes: Customer user tokens created by account/card admins in Dashboard > Developer (company must accept Developer API agreement), sent as Bearer; expire after 90 days unused. Partner OAuth 2.0/OIDC: authorization code (PKCE optional) for most APIs, client credentials for onboarding API; access tokens 1h, rotating refresh tokens 90 days; scopes like cards, cards.readonly, openid, offline_access.
access_notes: Partner OAuth client_id/secret are issued by contacting Brex developer support (not self-serve). User tokens are self-serve but only for existing Brex customer accounts. No public developer sandbox found.
api_breadth_notes: 10 API groups: Accounting, Budgets, Expenses, Fields, Onboarding, Payments, Team, Transactions, Travel, Webhooks; MCP exposes 44 tools. Exact endpoint count not verified.
mcp_notes: Official hosted beta server https://api.brex.com/mcp; OAuth with Dynamic Client Registration (auth server accounts-api.brex.com/oauth2/default) or Brex API token as Bearer; admin must accept API agreement and enable 'Brex in AI assistants' beta; 44 tools (expenses, users, cards, banking, bills, travel).
blocker: Needs Brex customer account; OAuth client issued via developer support
notes: A toolkit can work today with customer-supplied user tokens (Bearer), but multi-tenant OAuth requires Brex-issued partner credentials. https://developer.brex.com/docs/partner_authentication returned 404; the /guides/ path worked. Brex support page (https://www.brex.com/support/using-brex-in-ai-apps) says MCP is available to any account with Developer API access enabled. Card PAN/CVV not exposed via MCP.

one_liner: Corporate cards, expense management, bill pay and procurement platform for businesses.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0: client credentials (own business, server-to-server, 10-day tokens) and authorization code + refresh token for third-party apps (1h access tokens, 5-min codes). Scopes resource:read/write (~90 scopes); some restricted (cards:read_vault, partner-only scopes). Sandbox (demo.ramp.com) and production need separate apps.
access_notes: Ramp customers can create apps in the Developer Console for their own business. Third-party integrations: sandbox access by request, then a technology partnership application with security disclosures (SOC 2/ISO/pen test) and Ramp review; 'approval is required before production access'. Some endpoints also require specific Ramp plan features (403 otherwise).
api_breadth_notes: OpenAPI spec: 191 paths / 279 operations across ~44 groups (accounting, bills, cards, custom-records, vendors, transactions, reimbursements, users, purchase-orders, webhooks, etc.).
mcp_notes: Official hosted MCP https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp (sandbox https://demo-mcp.ramp.com/mcp); browser consent (OAuth-style), Full or Read-only access, connections expire after 30 days, admin-controlled permission. Also open-source local ramp-public/ramp_mcp using client ID/secret. Ramp recommends its CLI for coding agents.
blocker: Third-party production OAuth needs Ramp partnership approval and security review
notes: docs.ramp.com HTML pages are JS shells; machine-readable /llms-guides/*.txt and /openapi/developer-api.json work. The sandbox-access guide text was empty, so whether sandbox is instant or approval-based is unclear. Webhooks API includes create/verify/mock-event endpoints.

one_liner: Private capital market data on companies, deals, investors, funds and people.
auth_notes: Static key sent as 'Authorization: PB-Token {API_KEY}' to https://api.pitchbook.com; each call also consumes purchased API credits (402 when balance exhausted).
access_notes: API keys, credits and sandbox keys are provisioned through a PitchBook account manager/Customer Success Manager as part of a paid subscription add-on; no self-serve signup. Not every endpoint is included in every subscription.
api_breadth_notes: Seven data categories (Companies, Deals, People, Investors, Funds, Service Providers, Limited Partners); endpoint count not listed on fetched page.
mcp_notes: PitchBook Premium remote MCP https://premium.mcp.pitchbook.com/mcp published by PitchBook in Claude's connector directory (verified badge); sign-in required, for PitchBook clients; 24 tools. Separate PitchBook Essential MCP via Perplexity reported (not verified).
blocker: API keys and credits only via PitchBook sales contract
notes: Official help page https://pitchbook.com/help/pitchbook-api returned 403 to fetch; API details come from the Postman-hosted documentation that presents itself as PitchBook's. Per-call credit billing makes agent usage costly. Could be offered as bring-your-own-key for existing PitchBook API customers, but cannot be built or tested without a contract.
